pr_comments: Due to potential footguns regarding timed commands activating during the wrong state, I'm not interested in continuing this work. If someone is interested in taking up this work and solving that, go ahead!

issue_context.title: Add a `TimedCommands` `SystemParam` for easier delayed operations
comments:
> HOWEVER, developers might run into issues where entities get despawned or changed between the time when the command was queued and when it gets applied, so we should take care with what kinds of operations we allow through `TimedCommands`.

A deferred command can't assume that the world is in the same state as when it was issued, whether it runs later in the frame (`Commands`) or in a later frame (`TimedCommands`). The set of assumptions should be the same in both cases, so the same operations should all be valid IMO.

It's true that some bevy-provided commands currently behave improperly by panicking if the world has changed, and that bug will be triggered more frequently by `TimedCommands`. Those commands should be fixed, though.
Note that this needs to be part of bevy_time: bevy_ecs has no notion of time in this way.

What is the actual use case for this? Cause idk if you got this idea from the bug I encountered with `bevy_kira_audio` but that's a bug. Features shouldn't be added to work around bugs, bugs should be fixed.

I can't think of a context for this where it isn't just a foot gun. It's the equivalent of doing `sleep(duration)` in conventional engines. If this can be a 3rd party crate I think it would be more appropriate as a 3rd party crate.

> What is the actual use case for this? Cause idk if you got this idea from the bug I encountered with `bevy_kira_audio` but that's a bug. Features shouldn't be added to work around bugs, bugs should be fixed.
> 
> I can't think of a context for this where it isn't just a foot gun. It's the equivalent of doing `sleep(duration)` in conventional engines. If this can be a 3rd party crate I think it would be more appropriate as a 3rd party crate.

I can think of one or two contexts where this can be useful, many of them just for a visual appealing
Lets say for example that the user clicks a button, and I want to, exactly two seconds after, jumpscare the user with some kind of image or song. That would be very easy with TimedCommands
Another easy context for this is dialogs. There are times where I want to have some short time with nothing going on just to the crack up moment to come, something rather easy with TimedCommands
note that there are some other ways to accomplish the same thing, but IMO this helps the ergonomics very much.
